title: Pip and friends
scenario:
Oat Pals, a cereal brand, has an otter mascot named Pip. Your studio plans a short video series with Veo 3.1, and 30 matching still images. You build and protect the cast.

The cast sheet, the shot list and the check log in the exhibit are made up for this case.
exhibit:
Cast sheet draft (made up)
  Pip, otter mascot    front view approved; no side view yet
  Mina, freelance      one photo: laughing, lit from the left, wearing a hat
  Bo, dog              one pencil sketch
  Cereal box           packshot, front

Shot list (Veo 3.1, 8 seconds each)
  Shot 1  Pip and the cereal box
  Shot 2  Pip, Mina, Bo and the cereal box at a table

Check log for the stills (made up)
  Image 1 : scarf is red
  Image 20: scarf is orange
  Method  : each image was made from the image before it

questions.prompt: Shot 2 has four things that need a reference. Veo 3.1 takes up to three. What is the best plan?

options.text: Send all four reference images. The model will pick the three it likes best from the four.
options.explanation: Google lists up to 3 reference images for Veo 3.1. Nothing says the model chooses among extra ones.

options.text: Put Pip, Mina, Bo and the box into one collage image, and send it as a single reference.
options.explanation: Runway advises one subject per reference and warns against several competing subjects. A collage is exactly that.

options.text: Split it into two shots: Pip, Mina and the box, then Pip, Bo and the box. Three references each.
options.explanation: Right. The 3 slots are shared by people, characters and products, so plan the shots to fit them.

options.text: Use the limit of 4 characters from the Nano Banana notes, because that covers all four subjects.
options.explanation: That limit is for Google's image models. Veo 3.1 accepts up to 3 reference images, and the box is a product.

questions.prompt: What is the best fix for Mina's photo before it becomes her anchor?

options.text: Keep the laughing photo. A big expression gives life, and the model will tone it down when asked.
options.explanation: Runway says to choose a neutral expression unless you want a specific look carried through. A laugh and a hat would carry into every image.

options.text: Take a new photo, with her permission: clear, evenly lit, face visible, neutral expression.
options.explanation: Right. This matches Runway's advice for talent references, which we use for any tool, and it needs her permission first.

options.text: Keep the photo and add the words "neutral expression" to every prompt, so the look is not copied.
options.explanation: Runway's advice is about the reference itself. A look in the picture can carry through, so fix the picture.

options.text: Send a second photo with a different mood, so that the two moods cancel each other out.
options.explanation: Nothing in the docs says moods cancel out. It also breaks the rule of a clear, cohesive reference.

questions.prompt: The scarf is red in image 1 and orange in image 20. What is the best habit from now on?

options.text: Keep feeding each result into the next request, since the newest image is the latest version of Pip.
options.explanation: That is how small errors pile up, like a copy of a copy. Image 20 shows what happened.

options.text: Write "same scarf as before" in each prompt, and drop the sheet images to save input tokens.
options.explanation: A new request has no "before". The model needs the approved image to compare with.

options.text: Set quality to the highest value, because a higher quality keeps a character the same.
options.explanation: OpenAI lists consistency for recurring characters as a limit. Nothing links it to the quality setting.

options.text: Give the approved sheet image for each new asset, and compare the result with the anchor.
options.explanation: Right. This is our habit: return to the sheet, and check the result against the anchor.

questions.prompt: Which "never change" line works best for Pip's cast sheet entry?

options.text: Red scarf with a white stripe on the left, black ear tips, cream belly, round brown eyes.
options.explanation: Right. Google advises being hyper-specific. Each detail can be checked at a glance.

options.text: Keep Pip looking like Pip, with all the usual features from the approved front view.
options.explanation: This says nothing that a reviewer can check. It does not name a single feature.

options.text: A cute otter with a warm, friendly look that kids will love and remember for a long time.
options.explanation: This describes a feeling, not features. Two people would draw two different otters.

options.text: Same as in image 1, with a little more fun, and any scarf colour that fits the scene.
options.explanation: Letting the scarf colour change is the opposite of a never-change line.
